rationale: Option 0 explanation goes off target: "Most-to-least is a planned fading sequence that begins with an effective higher-assistance prompt; a single physical prompt alone does not establish that procedure." The option doesn't mention most-to-least. The first sentence alone is enough.

Option 1, "End the trial and move on to a different target for now", has confuses_with "prompt_fading". Ending a trial isn't confused with prompt fading; the nearer concept is error correction or trial termination. The tag abandons_prompt_hierarchy_after_nonresponse itself fits.

Key "Give the gesture prompt, the next step in the hierarchy" restates the rule ("next step in the hierarchy") and is the only option that refers back to the stem's hierarchy. A test-wise reader can pick it without knowing least-to-most. Suggest "Give a gesture prompt".

Option 2, "Nothing changes, since extinction was in place for most of the session", is tagged abandons_extinction_during_burst (confuses_with extinction_burst). Someone choosing it isn't abandoning extinction. They believe consistent extinction for most of a session cancels out one reinforced instance, which is a misunderstanding of intermittent reinforcement. This also inflates abandons_extinction_during_burst from 1 to 2 items.

Option 2 remediation, "report inconsistent implementation and follow the plan's safety and stopping rules during escalation; extinction never overrides immediate safety", is about safety and reporting. It never corrects the error behind the option (that one attention delivery after screaming can strengthen screaming).

Same scenario frame as item 35: "extinction for attention-maintained whining" that gets louder early in extinction (35: "second day", 1439: "first day"). Stem TF-IDF cosine 0.40. The questions differ (what to do vs predicted effect), so keep both, but put them in one surface_cluster so neither counts as a fresh opportunity after the other.

Option 0, "Whining will decrease, since the coworker only gave in once", is tagged delivers_reinforcer_after_problem_behavior. That's an implementer-action tag on a prediction option (the learner's belief is that a single reinforcement doesn't matter). The remediation ("consequences can reinforce problem behavior") does fit, so low.
The key explanation adds action advice to a predicted-effect question: "Report the inconsistency and follow the written safety and stopping rules." It's accurate but not what was asked.

Option 0, "The design is invalid, because multielement designs cannot compare two treatments", is a belief about what the design can do, but it's tagged misreads_multielement_data with remediation "separation of data paths = differential effect". Neither names that error. It also leaves misreads_multielement_data on 2 of 3 distractors.

Option 1, "The first procedure introduced is more effective, because it was used first". In an alternating-treatments design, conditions are rapidly alternated, so few prepared candidates would treat order of first introduction as evidence. Pick-rate data will confirm.

Option 2, "They need no baseline, so the procedure can start right away", is tagged attributes_effect_without_control. The error is about baseline logic, and the bank already has confuses_baseline_logic_elements (used in item 2074 option 1), which fits better.

One pointer, "Review D.6: interpreting single-case data", serves three different tags (misapplies_changing_criterion, rejects_interpretable_data, attributes_effect_without_control). Option 1's pointer should name changing-criterion logic (behavior tracking each criterion step).

Key "Choose students who will not see or hear the program before their own start" fixes the problem by swapping participants. The more common fix is to change delivery (run each student's sessions where untreated students can't observe). It's still the best of the four options. Suggest: "Arrange delivery so untreated students are not exposed to the program before their own start".

Option 3, "Control is not shown, since the baseline phase had too little variability", is tagged rejects_interpretable_data. The learner reaches the right conclusion for the wrong reason (believing a stable baseline is a weakness); its own confuses_with is baseline_stability. A baseline-logic tag fits better. Its pointer is also shared with option 0 (generic).
Option 3, "Carry 9 tokens forward by adding the sticker's 2-token price". Adding a purchase price to the balance is unlikely to attract anyone who read the stem.
Labeled "hard", but the key is one arithmetic step (4 + 3 - 2 = 5) plus reading the carryover rule. Expect a high p-value. Re-band once n≥100.

Key "Clarify the request and contact the BCBA before using the token board again" has the RBT stop a written procedure before any BCBA direction. The justification ("do not continue the disputed token board over the objection") is in the explanation only; the stem frames the parent's words as a preference ("We're trying a sticker chart at home instead"), not a withdrawal of consent. A BCBA could reasonably key "keep the plan as written for now, tell the parent you'll pass it on, and contact the BCBA today". SME to rule, then either add the consent fact to the stem or rewrite the key.

Conflicts with item 40 as written. Item 40 option 2's explanation says "Stopping a program without direction is also an unapproved change", while 37 keys not using the token board until the BCBA is contacted. Both are tagged changes_plan_without_supervisor. The caregiver-objection distinction may justify the difference, but the learner-facing text doesn't state it, so the learner gets two rules that seem to clash.
"BACB RBT Ethics Code (2.0), Sections 2.02, 2.06, 2.07". I could not verify the section numbers against the code's text from here. Verify once in a citation registry, not per item.
"BACB RBT Ethics Code (2.0), Section 2.06": section number not verified. Same registry check as items 37 and 40.

All 3 distractors carry changes_plan_without_supervisor, so a wrong answer reveals nothing more specific. Option 1, "Lower the mastery criterion a little so he can pass", is described by its own explanation as something that "would misrepresent progress". Existing tags alters_or_discards_data or inflates_assessment_results fit it more specifically.
"BACB RBT Ethics Code (2.0), Section 2.02, 2.06": section numbers not verified, and the format should read "Sections" (compare item 37).

Option 2, "Cancel token opportunities for the remaining session after this occurrence", is tagged changes_plan_without_supervisor, but its explanation says it "would add a consequence not specified in the plan". Item 35 tags the same kind of error ("Add a consequence of your own") as adds_unplanned_procedure. Tag the same error the same way everywhere.

The stem spells out both rules the distractors' traps depend on ("only if no spitting occurred anywhere in that interval; spitting does not change the scheduled boundaries"). So options 0 (resetting_dro) and 1 (momentary_dro) test reading compliance, not whether the learner can tell DRO variants apart. That matters if this item counts as evidence for confuses_differential_reinforcement_types. SME: intended (an RBT follows the written plan), or weaken the stem to "nonresetting whole-interval DRO" alone for a discrimination version.
